**Final answer: 18.83%** (pooled gap characters / total alignment positions across all 10 alignments). Secondary metric (mean of per-file percentages): **18.25%**.

This value comes from a pure-Python re-implementation that approximates MAFFT `--auto` (L-INS-i analog: BLOSUM62, gap-open 1.53, gap-extend 0, UPGMA guide tree + progressive profile alignment, `-` as gap char), because the real MAFFT binary is **not installed in this environment** (verified exhaustively: not on PATH/filesystem, no apt/conda/pip path, no network). Gap counting is exactly as agreed: gap = `-` only; positions = nseq × width (cells); "across all alignments" = pooling (`100 × Σgaps / Σ(nseq×width)` = 100 × 3,204 / 17,013).

Important execution note (transparency): during execution I found and fixed two real bugs in my first implementation — (1) a sign error (gap penalties were being *added* to the DP score instead of subtracted) and (2) a broken traceback (following recomputed cell argmaxes instead of stored pointers, which could drift off the optimal path). Both would have inflated the answer (a buggy intermediate run gave 28.6%). After the fixes, the DP was validated against an independent constrained affine-gap brute-force enumerator: **0 mismatches over 400 random pairs** and **0 traceback-score inconsistencies**, and all 10 output alignments pass consistency checks (rectangular widths, only `-`/standard AA characters, every input residue preserved, no all-gap columns). The reported 18.83% is the faithful optimum of the agreed BLOSUM62/1.53/0.0 objective.
